title: A｜山墙老客栈
adopted_prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: original architecture/environment concept board for the first-person mystery game 《错日证词》, fictional Qingchuan small town, January 1931, no actual country assigned.
Primary request: ONE complete design concept for a playable small-town HOTEL / INN, one of five different alternatives. High quality landscape architectural game-art presentation sheet.
Composition: elegant narrow cream margins, exact short Chinese scheme title at top. One large exterior three-quarter establishing view across the upper 42%, showing the ENTIRE hotel massing including full roof ridge and chimneys, open sky margin, ground and entrance/arrival court. Lower portion arranged as four balanced panels in a 2x2 grid: immersive eye-level registration lobby, immersive dining room, clearly readable roof-removed axonometric of ground-floor layout, and separate roof-removed upper-floor guest-room layout aligned to the same footprint. Text labels only “外观”, “登记大堂”, “餐厅”, “一层示意”, “二层客房”. No extra captions, measurements, legends or prose. Floor views should show sufficient detail and clear circulation, not miniatures too small to read.
Style: richly crafted modeled 3D game environment concept art, restrained stylization, believable scale and tactile materials, carefully composed cinematic lighting. NOT toy blocks, NOT a modern real-estate advertising render, NOT a horror ruin. Match the existing game's cream plaster, low saturation greys/greens, aged oak and walnut, old iron and brass, blue-violet exterior shadows and warm amber practical lamps. Winter bare deciduous trees, damp paved ground, soft overcast dusk; no snow, no summer bloom. Interior detail remains readable, not crushed black.
Shared playable program: modest independent inn within roughly a 41m by 40m town parcel including arrival court, TWO usable floors, about eight to twelve guest rooms. Ground floor directly accessible registration lobby and reception counter with wooden key pigeonholes; public-side low writing desk with a guest registration ledger whose pages can be examined under an adjustable shaded lamp, a modest porter/concierge nook near the entrance with view onto the arrival court, luggage stand, waiting chairs, separate dining room, dining-room cashier/ledger desk, kitchen and pantry behind dining, modest manager office and linen store, service delivery door and rear path. A genuine continuous staircase to upper guest corridor; guest bedrooms with simple timber beds, period wardrobe, basin stand and small washroom area. Any upper-floor facade window must correspond to usable space; any balcony must connect to an actual guest corridor or room. Keep entrances, windows, staircase and footprint reasonably consistent across views.
Arrival court: broad ground-level path for walking and a small 1928–31 unbranded dark chestnut-red four-door sedan with black fenders belonging to the hotel, parked off the pedestrian entrance route, optional small luggage canopy. No vehicle blocking doors, no stairs across driving path, no enormous carriage palace.
Narrative: this inn hosts a BRIEF stay, not a murder scene. The guest ledger, dining account and porter's recollection are narrative investigation sources. Show folded/cross-page paper and mild ink wear as period prop detail, but all page text is indistinct blank lines. Do NOT invent guest names, readable dates/times, clue answers, itinerary maps, a confirmed alibi, a suspect room, blood or police evidence boards. The hotel car is an existing environmental asset, not an additional historical clue. No clocks or calendar displays in any view, no automatic time clues.
Period restrictions: early 1930s furnishings, wooden key rack and paper ledgers, small mechanical desk bell, leather luggage, bronze shaded lamps and warm opal ceiling lights. No computers, electric neon sign, LED displays, plastic furniture, air conditioners, CCTV, TV, elevator, modern car, modern exit/safety sign, logos, flags or national emblems. No characters necessary. On-building sign may only say “旅馆”.
Architecture-specific direction and exact title follow.

Exact header: “A · 山墙老客栈”.
A: a historic two-storey street inn formed by three unequal adjoining gabled volumes, dark walnut exposed timber framing with warm cream infill, rough buff stone ground-floor plinth, steep dark slate roofs, deep projecting eaves and small authentic upper casement windows. Main asymmetrical timber entrance porch faces a compact paved drop-off court; two wings continue to rear around a small service garden, not an enclosed cloister. Human-scale, cozy, irregular roof silhouette, village merchant lodging rather than Tudor fantasy castle. Full roofs and chimney tops visible in the exterior view. Lobby has old exposed beams, polished dark wood curved reception, worn patterned rug over timber boards, brass lamp over a broadly usable side writing desk, simple keyholes/pigeonholes behind counter; dining room feels like a warm low-beamed common room with six small round tables, plain chairs, cream curtains and a working fireplace. Upper corridor passes actual simple guest rooms beneath the gables. Materials dominate, no big glass facade, no formal symmetry or stone arcade.

D: intimate U-shaped TWO-storey inn embracing an OPEN-TO-SKY paved central arrival court, warm light grey/buff limestone lower walls, pale lime plaster upper walls, burgundy timber doors, low grey hipped slate roofs, ground-floor sheltered stone-arch loggias and a slender timber balustrade gallery at the courtyard's upper level.
